description: CPU benchmark of every compressed variant of the fine-tuned PardaDB GLiNER PII model (benchmark.py, 4 threads, threshold from reports/ft.json). Bank = 800-text held-out bank test set (micro F1), golden = hand-written golden set (micro F1), Saffron recall on n=400 real customer names and n=400 transaction narrations (never trained on). cpu_ms_per_text = median over 50 batches of 16 after 2 warm-up batches. Sizes in MB = 1e6 bytes; dir_mb includes tokenizer and config. Peak RSS is the whole Python process (about 756 MB of it is Python + torch + gliner before any model loads).

env.gpu: unavailable (driver down); all numbers are CPU

rationale: int8w (format int8-weight) is the chosen model: the only sub-100 MB variant that is both independently re-verified and at least as accurate as float32 on every metric. Its weights file is 45.4 MB (49.0 MB for the whole directory with tokenizer and config) against 180.7 MB for the float32 checkpoint, 4.0x smaller, with bank micro F1 0.988 vs 0.984, golden F1 0.939 vs 0.936, Saffron name recall 0.998 (equal) and narration recall 0.948 vs 0.935. Every large matrix, including the 19.3 M-parameter token embedding, is stored as symmetric per-output-channel int8 with float16 scales (worst reconstruction error 0.39% of a tensor's absmax); it is dequantized to float32 at load, so CPU compute and speed match float32 (about 18 ms per text on 4 threads) and the sidecar holds about 0.98 GB RSS after load. A rebuild from models/pardadb-pii is byte-identical. Alternatives: onnx-int8-fp16 is 1.5x faster on CPU (11.2 ms/text) at 58.6 MB with bank F1 0.988 and golden 0.935, but was not independently re-verified; int8w-dyn reads the same 45.4 MB file and runs part of the encoder in int8 for about 51 MB less RAM and 11-18% more speed, at bank F1 0.984 (equal to fp32) and golden 0.938. Naive dynamic int8 of every Linear layer (114 MB, bank F1 0.773) and per-channel ONNX int8 of every weight (F1 0.0) failed because they quantize activations of the outlier-heavy GeGLU and QKV layers.
size_note: The float32 fine-tuned checkpoint that was compressed is 180.7 MB on disk (45.18 M parameters). Peak process memory of the float32 CPU sidecar is about 1.15 GB; the int8 variants change disk size, not that peak.

variants.verification: reference run; accuracy identical to the GPU numbers in reports/ft.json

variants.notes: Disk saving only; weights upcast to float32 at load.

variants.verification: independent re-run in a fresh process (reports/compression/int8w.verify.json): identical accuracy and sizes; standalone load traced with strace
variants.notes: CHOSEN. Per-output-channel int8 weights (embeddings, encoder, LSTM, scorer) with float16 scales; dequantized to float32 at load.

variants.verification: independent re-run in a fresh process (reports/compression/int8w-dyn.verify.json): identical accuracy
variants.notes: Same file as int8w; encoder attn.Wo/mlp.Wi run as torch dynamic int8. ~51 MB less RAM after load, 11-18% faster than fp32 under the same load.
Fastest: ONNX Runtime, int8 embeddings/LSTM/scorer, encoder stored float16. 1.5x faster than torch fp32. Not independently re-verified.
Int8 except MLP down-projections; just inside the 0.01 bank budget but loses organization F1 and narration recall.
Encoder float32; same predictions as onnx-int8-fp16, 26 MB larger.
Export check only, no quantization; identical accuracy to torch fp32.
FAILED: per-channel int8 on every weight predicts nothing (F1 0.0). Kept as a record.
